1 | """Shared data loading and cleaning utilities.
  2 | 
  3 | This module is the single source of truth for reading and preparing the
  4 | project's raw CSV datasets. Analysis scripts should import their loaders from
  5 | here instead of reading the CSVs directly, so that parsing and cleaning rules
  6 | stay consistent across the whole project.
  7 | 
  8 | The raw files carry a UTF-8 BOM and store money as ``€``-formatted strings
  9 | (e.g. ``"€13,940.00"``); this module strips the BOM, parses those strings into
 10 | floats, coerces the numeric columns, and assigns sensible dtypes (nullable
 11 | integers/floats and categoricals) while preserving missing values. Values that
 12 | are legitimately absent ("not applicable") are marked with the string ``"NA"``
 13 | so they can be told apart from genuinely missing values (``pd.NA``). An
 14 | optional listwise-deletion step (:func:`drop_missing_rows`) removes rows with
 15 | genuinely missing values while leaving the ``"NA"`` markers intact.
 16 | """
 17 | 
 18 | from __future__ import annotations
 19 | 
 20 | from collections.abc import Sequence
 21 | from pathlib import Path
 22 | from typing import Any
 23 | 
 24 | import numpy as np
 25 | import pandas as pd
 26 | 
 27 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 28 | # Paths
 29 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 30 | PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
 31 | DATA_DIR = PROJECT_ROOT / "data"
 32 | 
 33 | HISTORICAL_DATA_FILENAME = "historical_data.csv"
 34 | DATA_DICTIONARY_FILENAME = "data_dictionary.csv"
 35 | 
 36 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 37 | # Column metadata for historical_data.csv
 38 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 39 | CATEGORICAL_COLUMNS: list[str] = [
 40 |     "Category",
 41 |     "Innovation_Type",
 42 |     "Research_Package",
 43 |     "Recommendation",
 44 | ]
 45 | 
 46 | INTEGER_COLUMNS: list[str] = ["Test_Year", "Sample_Size", "Turnaround_Days"]
 47 | 
 48 | BINARY_COLUMNS: list[str] = ["Launched"]
 49 | 
 50 | CURRENCY_COLUMNS: list[str] = ["Research_Cost_EUR", "Launch_Support_EUR"]
 51 | 
 52 | FLOAT_COLUMNS: list[str] = [
 53 |     "Stated_Appeal",
 54 |     "Purchase_Intent",
 55 |     "Behavioural_Choice_Pct",
 56 |     "Implicit_Score",
 57 |     "Distribution_Pct",
 58 |     "Sales_vs_Target_Pct",
 59 |     "Repeat_Purchase_Pct",
 60 | ]
 61 | 
 62 | TEXT_COLUMNS: list[str] = ["Concept_ID"]
 63 | 
 64 | #: Marker used for values that are legitimately absent ("not applicable"),
 65 | #: distinct from genuinely missing values (``pd.NA``).
 66 | NA_MARKER: str = "NA"
 67 | 
 68 | #: Columns that are only applicable under a condition. Their legitimately
 69 | #: absent ("not applicable") values are replaced with :data:`NA_MARKER` during
 70 | #: cleaning so they can be told apart from genuinely missing values.
 71 | CONDITIONAL_COLUMNS: list[str] = [
 72 |     "Behavioural_Choice_Pct",
 73 |     "Implicit_Score",
 74 |     "Launch_Support_EUR",
 75 |     "Distribution_Pct",
 76 |     "Sales_vs_Target_Pct",
 77 |     "Repeat_Purchase_Pct",
 78 | ]
 79 | 
 80 | 
 81 | def _not_applicable(df: pd.DataFrame, column: str) -> pd.Series:
 82 |     """Return a boolean mask of cells whose value is legitimately absent.
 83 | 
 84 |     A cell is "not applicable" when the concept's design means the metric was
 85 |     never meant to be collected (e.g. launch metrics for unlaunched concepts).
 86 |     """
 87 |     if column == "Behavioural_Choice_Pct":
 88 |         return ~df["Research_Package"].isin(["Behavioural", "Combined"])
 89 |     if column == "Implicit_Score":
 90 |         return df["Research_Package"] != "Combined"
 91 |     if column in (
 92 |         "Launch_Support_EUR",
 93 |         "Distribution_Pct",
 94 |         "Sales_vs_Target_Pct",
 95 |         "Repeat_Purchase_Pct",
 96 |     ):
 97 |         return df["Launched"] != 1
 98 |     return pd.Series(False, index=df.index)
 99 | 
100 | 
101 | def correlation_strength(r: float) -> str:
102 |     """Classify a correlation coefficient into a strength band.
103 | 
104 |     Bands: |r| < 0.20 negligible, 0.20–0.29 weak, 0.30–0.49 moderate, ≥ 0.50
105 |     strong.
106 |     """
107 |     r_abs = abs(r)
108 |     if r_abs >= 0.50:
109 |         return "Strong"
110 |     if r_abs >= 0.30:
111 |         return "Moderate"
112 |     if r_abs >= 0.20:
113 |         return "Weak"
114 |     return "Negligible"
115 | 
116 | 
117 | def get_data_path(filename: str) -> Path:
118 |     """Return the absolute path to ``filename`` inside the ``data/`` directory."""
119 |     return DATA_DIR / filename
120 | 
121 | 
122 | def read_csv(path: str | Path, **kwargs: Any) -> pd.DataFrame:
123 |     """Read a CSV with the project's standard defaults.
124 | 
125 |     The source files carry a UTF-8 BOM, so they are decoded with ``utf-8-sig``.
126 |     Empty cells are treated as missing values (pandas default).
127 |     """
128 |     defaults: dict[str, Any] = {"encoding": "utf-8-sig"}
129 |     defaults.update(kwargs)
130 |     return pd.read_csv(path, **defaults)
131 | 
132 | 
133 | def parse_currency(value: Any) -> float | None:
134 |     """Convert a ``€``-formatted string such as ``"€13,940.00"`` to a float.
135 | 
136 |     Returns ``None`` for missing/blank values so the result can be stored in a
137 |     nullable float column. Already-numeric values are passed through unchanged.
138 |     """
139 |     if pd.isna(value):
140 |         return None
141 |     if isinstance(value, (int, float, np.integer, np.floating)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
142 |         return float(value)
143 |     text = (
144 |         str(value)
145 |         .replace("€", "")
146 |         .replace("\u20ac", "")
147 |         .replace(",", "")
148 |         .replace("\u00a0", "")
149 |         .strip()
150 |     )
151 |     if text == "":
152 |         return None
153 |     try:
154 |         return float(text)
155 |     except ValueError:
156 |         return None
157 | 
158 | 
159 | def clean_historical_data(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
160 |     """Clean and type a freshly loaded historical dataset.
161 | 
162 |     Returns a copy of ``df`` with:
163 | 
164 |     * column names trimmed of whitespace,
165 |     * ``€``-formatted currency columns parsed into nullable floats,
166 |     * numeric columns coerced to nullable ``Float64`` / ``Int64``,
167 |     * categorical columns cast to ``category`` (with whitespace trimmed),
168 |     * the ``Concept_ID`` text column trimmed and stored as ``string``,
169 |     * "not applicable" values replaced with the ``"NA"`` marker so they are
170 |       distinguishable from genuinely missing values (``pd.NA``).
171 |     """
172 |     df = df.copy()
173 |     df.columns = [str(column).strip() for column in df.columns]
174 | 
175 |     for column in CURRENCY_COLUMNS:
176 |         if column in df.columns:
177 |             df[column] = df[column].map(parse_currency).astype("Float64")
178 | 
179 |     for column in FLOAT_COLUMNS:
180 |         if column in df.columns:
181 |             df[column] = pd.to_numeric(df[column], errors="coerce").astype("Float64")
182 | 
183 |     for column in INTEGER_COLUMNS + BINARY_COLUMNS:
184 |         if column in df.columns:
185 |             df[column] = pd.to_numeric(df[column], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
186 | 
187 |     for column in CATEGORICAL_COLUMNS:
188 |         if column in df.columns:
189 |             df[column] = (
190 |                 df[column].astype("string").str.strip().replace({"": pd.NA}).astype("category")
191 |             )
192 | 
193 |     for column in TEXT_COLUMNS:
194 |         if column in df.columns:
195 |             df[column] = df[column].astype("string").str.strip()
196 | 
197 |     # Replace "not applicable" (absent by design) values with the "NA" marker
198 |     # so they are distinguishable from genuinely missing values (pd.NA). Cast
199 |     # to object first so the column can hold both numbers and the "NA" string.
200 |     for column in CONDITIONAL_COLUMNS:
201 |         if column in df.columns:
202 |             not_applicable = _not_applicable(df, column)
203 |             df[column] = df[column].astype(object).mask(not_applicable, NA_MARKER)
204 | 
205 |     return df
206 | 
207 | 
208 | def drop_missing_rows(
209 |     df: pd.DataFrame, columns: Sequence[str] | None = None
210 | ) -> pd.DataFrame:
211 |     """Drop rows with genuinely missing values in ``columns`` (listwise deletion).
212 | 
213 |     Only truly missing values (``pd.NA``) are treated as missing; structural
214 |     ``"NA"`` (absent by design) markers are valid and are left intact.
215 | 
216 |     * ``columns=None`` — full listwise deletion: drop rows missing in *any*
217 |       column.
218 |     * ``columns=[...]`` — per-model deletion: drop rows only when one of the
219 |       listed columns is missing, leaving missingness in other columns intact.
220 | 
221 |     Returns a new DataFrame.
222 |     """
223 |     if columns is None:
224 |         return df.dropna()
225 |     columns = list(columns)
226 |     if not columns:
227 |         return df.copy()
228 |     return df.dropna(subset=columns)
229 | 
230 | 
231 | def load_historical_data(
232 |     path: str | Path | None = None,
233 |     *,
234 |     clean: bool = True,
235 |     drop_missing: bool | Sequence[str] = False,
236 | ) -> pd.DataFrame:
237 |     """Load (and, by default, clean) the historical concept-test dataset.
238 | 
239 |     ``drop_missing`` controls listwise deletion after cleaning:
240 | 
241 |     * ``False`` (default) — no rows are dropped.
242 |     * ``True`` — full listwise deletion (rows missing in any column).
243 |     * a sequence of column names — per-model deletion (rows missing in any of
244 |       those columns only).
245 | 
246 |     Only truly missing values (``pd.NA``) are treated as missing; structural
247 |     ``"NA"`` (absent by design) values are never deleted. Deletion relies on
248 |     the ``"NA"`` markers, so cleaning is implicitly enabled whenever
249 |     ``drop_missing`` is not ``False``.
250 |     """
251 |     source = Path(path) if path is not None else get_data_path(HISTORICAL_DATA_FILENAME)
252 |     df = read_csv(source)
253 |     if clean or drop_missing is not False:
254 |         df = clean_historical_data(df)
255 |     if drop_missing is True:
256 |         df = drop_missing_rows(df)
257 |     elif drop_missing is not False:
258 |         df = drop_missing_rows(df, columns=drop_missing)
259 |     return df
260 | 
261 | 
262 | def load_data_dictionary(path: str | Path | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
263 |     """Load the data dictionary (column-level metadata) with whitespace trimmed."""
264 |     source = Path(path) if path is not None else get_data_path(DATA_DICTIONARY_FILENAME)
265 |     df = read_csv(source)
266 |     df.columns = [str(column).strip() for column in df.columns]
267 |     for column in df.columns:
268 |         if df[column].dtype == object:
269 |             df[column] = df[column].astype("string").str.strip().replace({"": pd.NA})
270 |     return df
271 | 
272 | 
273 | __all__ = [
274 |     "CONDITIONAL_COLUMNS",
275 |     "DATA_DIR",
276 |     "NA_MARKER",
277 |     "PROJECT_ROOT",
278 |     "clean_historical_data",
279 |     "correlation_strength",
280 |     "drop_missing_rows",
281 |     "get_data_path",
282 |     "load_data_dictionary",
283 |     "load_historical_data",
284 |     "parse_currency",
285 |     "read_csv",
286 | ]
287 | 
288 | 
289 | if __name__ == "__main__":
290 |     historical = load_historical_data()
291 |     dictionary = load_data_dictionary()
292 | 
293 |     print("Historical data shape:", historical.shape)
294 |     print("\nDtypes:\n", historical.dtypes)
295 |     print("\nMissing values per column:\n", historical.isna().sum())
296 |     print("\nHead:\n", historical.head())
297 |     print("\nData dictionary:\n", dictionary)

  5 | first linear model, and records the caveats that bound interpretation. Writes to
  6 | ``output/logs/modelling.md``.

 41 | def _context_facts(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, float | int]:
 42 |     """Compute the small set of data facts referenced by the caveats."""
 43 |     # Implicit_Score subsample (Combined packages only).
 44 |     implicit = df[df["Research_Package"] == "Combined"]
 45 |     implicit_complete = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(implicit, ["Implicit_Score"])
 46 | 
 47 |     # Collinearity between the research-economics metrics.
 48 |     cost_days = df[["Research_Cost_EUR", "Turnaround_Days"]].apply(
 49 |         pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce"
 50 |     )
 51 | 
 52 |     # Package-mix shift 2022 -> 2025.
 53 |     package_pct = (
 54 |         pd.crosstab(df["Test_Year"], df["Research_Package"])
 55 |         .div(pd.crosstab(df["Test_Year"], df["Research_Package"]).sum(axis=1), axis=0)
 56 |         * 100
 57 |     )
 58 | 
 59 |     return {
 60 |         "n_implicit_applicable": len(implicit),
 61 |         "n_implicit_complete": len(implicit_complete),
 62 |         "implicit_missing_rate": (len(implicit) - len(implicit_complete))
 63 |         / len(implicit)
 64 |         * 100,
 65 |         "r_cost_days": float(cost_days.corr().iloc[0, 1]),
 66 |         "survey_2022": package_pct.loc[2022, "Survey"],
 67 |         "survey_2025": package_pct.loc[2025, "Survey"],
 68 |     }

 71 | def _package_success(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
 72 |     """Compare binary success across research packages (Survey baseline).
 73 | 
 74 |     Restricted to launched concepts with an observed ``Sales_vs_Target_Pct``.
 75 |     """
 76 |     launched = df[df["Launched"] == 1].copy()
 77 |     launched["sales"] = pd.to_numeric(launched["Sales_vs_Target_Pct"], errors="coerce")
 78 |     sub = launched[launched["sales"].notna()].copy()
 79 |     sub["success"] = (sub["sales"] >= SUCCESS_THRESHOLD).astype(int)
 80 | 
 81 |     ct = pd.crosstab(sub["Research_Package"], sub["success"])
 82 |     chi2, p, dof, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(ct)
 83 | 
 84 |     success_rate = ct[1] / ct.sum(axis=1) * 100
 85 |     n = ct.sum(axis=1)
 86 | 
 87 |     cost = launched.groupby("Research_Package", observed=True)["Research_Cost_EUR"].apply(
 88 |         lambda s: pd.to_numeric(s, errors="coerce").mean()
 89 |     )
 90 |     days = launched.groupby("Research_Package", observed=True)["Turnaround_Days"].apply(
 91 |         lambda s: pd.to_numeric(s, errors="coerce").mean()
 92 |     )
 93 | 
 94 |     base_success = success_rate["Survey"]
 95 |     base_cost = cost["Survey"]
 96 |     base_days = days["Survey"]
 97 | 
 98 |     rows = []
 99 |     for package in ["Survey", "Behavioural", "Combined"]:
100 |         rows.append(
101 |             {
102 |                 "Research package": package,
103 |                 "n": int(n[package]),
104 |                 "Success rate (%)": f"{success_rate[package]:.1f}",
105 |                 "Δ success vs Survey (pp)": (
106 |                     "—" if package == "Survey" else f"{success_rate[package] - base_success:+.1f}"
107 |                 ),
108 |                 "Δ cost vs Survey (€)": (
109 |                     "—" if package == "Survey" else f"{cost[package] - base_cost:+,.0f}"
110 |                 ),
111 |                 "Δ turnaround vs Survey (days)": (
112 |                     "—" if package == "Survey" else f"{days[package] - base_days:+.1f}"
113 |                 ),
114 |             }
115 |         )
116 | 
117 |     return {
118 |         "table": pd.DataFrame(rows),
119 |         "n_launched": int(len(launched)),
120 |         "n_complete": int(len(sub)),
121 |         "n_missing_target": int(launched["sales"].isna().sum()),
122 |         "overall_success": float(sub["success"].mean() * 100),
123 |         "chi2": float(chi2),
124 |         "p": float(p),
125 |         "dof": int(dof),
126 |         "success_rate": {pkg: float(success_rate[pkg]) for pkg in ["Survey", "Behavioural", "Combined"]},
127 |         "delta_pp": {pkg: float(success_rate[pkg] - base_success) for pkg in ["Behavioural", "Combined"]},
128 |     }

131 | def _applicable_mask(df: pd.DataFrame, columns: list[str]) -> pd.Series:
132 |     """Rows where every conditional column is applicable (not the NA marker)."""
133 |     mask = pd.Series(True, index=df.index)
134 |     for column in columns:
135 |         if column in data_utilities.CONDITIONAL_COLUMNS:
136 |             mask &= ~df[column].eq(data_utilities.NA_MARKER).fillna(False)
137 |     return mask

140 | def linear_model(
141 |     df: pd.DataFrame,
142 |     predictors: list[str],
143 |     complete_on: list[str] | None = None,
144 | ) -> dict:
145 |     """Fit a linear regression of the target on ``predictors``.
146 | 
147 |     Restricted to launched concepts (the target is launch-phase only), to rows
148 |     where the ``complete_on`` columns are applicable, and to per-model complete
149 |     cases on ``complete_on`` and the target. ``complete_on`` defaults to
150 |     ``predictors``; pass it explicitly to refit a model on a fixed subset.
151 |     """
152 |     if complete_on is None:
153 |         complete_on = predictors
154 |     launched = df[df["Launched"] == 1]
155 |     launched = launched[_applicable_mask(launched, complete_on)]
156 |     sub = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(launched, complete_on + [TARGET])
157 | 
158 |     X = pd.DataFrame(
159 |         {col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in predictors}
160 |     )
161 |     y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce")
162 | 
163 |     model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
164 |     n = len(X)
165 |     k = len(predictors)
166 |     r2 = float(model.score(X, y))
167 |     adj_r2 = 1 - (1 - r2) * (n - 1) / (n - k - 1)
168 | 
169 |     coefs = pd.DataFrame(
170 |         [{"Term": "Intercept", "Coefficient": float(model.intercept_)}]
171 |         + [
172 |             {"Term": col, "Coefficient": float(coef)}
173 |             for col, coef in zip(predictors, model.coef_)
174 |         ]
175 |     )
176 | 
177 |     return {
178 |         "n": n,
179 |         "r2": r2,
180 |         "adj_r2": adj_r2,
181 |         "coefs": coefs,
182 |         "coef": dict(zip(predictors, model.coef_.tolist())),
183 |         "y": y.to_numpy(),
184 |         "y_pred": model.predict(X),
185 |     }

188 | def ridge_model(
189 |     df: pd.DataFrame,
190 |     predictors: list[str],
191 |     complete_on: list[str] | None = None,
192 |     alpha: float | None = None,
193 | ) -> dict:
194 |     """Fit a ridge regression of the target on ``predictors``.
195 | 
196 |     Predictors are standardised to z-scores so the L2 penalty treats each
197 |     variable equally. When ``alpha`` is ``None`` (default) the regularisation
198 |     strength is selected by leave-one-out cross-validation (``RidgeCV``);
199 |     otherwise a fixed ``alpha`` is used. Passing ``alpha=0.0`` recovers an
200 |     unregularised OLS fit on the standardised predictors, giving per-SD
201 |     coefficients directly comparable with the ridge ones. The sample is
202 |     restricted exactly like :func:`linear_model`.
203 |     """
204 |     if complete_on is None:
205 |         complete_on = predictors
206 |     launched = df[df["Launched"] == 1]
207 |     launched = launched[_applicable_mask(launched, complete_on)]
208 |     sub = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(launched, complete_on + [TARGET])
209 | 
210 |     X = pd.DataFrame(
211 |         {col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in predictors}
212 |     )
213 |     y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce")
214 | 
215 |     scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X)
216 |     X_std = pd.DataFrame(scaler.transform(X), columns=predictors)
217 | 
218 |     if alpha is None:
219 |         model = RidgeCV(alphas=RIDGE_ALPHAS).fit(X_std, y)
220 |     else:
221 |         model = Ridge(alpha=alpha).fit(X_std, y)
222 |     n = len(X)
223 |     r2 = float(model.score(X_std, y))
224 | 
225 |     coefs = pd.DataFrame(
226 |         [{"Term": "Intercept", "Coefficient": float(model.intercept_)}]
227 |         + [
228 |             {"Term": col, "Coefficient": float(coef)}
229 |             for col, coef in zip(predictors, model.coef_)
230 |         ]
231 |     )
232 | 
233 |     return {
234 |         "n": n,
235 |         "r2": r2,
236 |         "alpha": float(model.alpha_) if alpha is None else float(alpha),
237 |         "coefs": coefs,
238 |         "coef": dict(zip(predictors, model.coef_.tolist())),
239 |         "y": y.to_numpy(),
240 |         "y_pred": model.predict(X_std),
241 |     }

244 | def _prepare_xy(
245 |     df: pd.DataFrame, predictors: list[str], years: list[int]
246 | ) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
247 |     """Restrict to launched concepts in ``years`` with applicable + complete data.
248 | 
249 |     Returns the numeric predictor matrix ``X`` and target ``y``. Structural
250 |     ``"NA"`` markers are excluded via the applicability mask, then genuinely
251 |     missing values (``pd.NA``) are dropped per-model on the predictors and the
252 |     target.
253 |     """
254 |     sub = df[(df["Test_Year"].isin(years)) & (df["Launched"] == 1)]
255 |     sub = sub[_applicable_mask(sub, predictors)]
256 |     sub = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(sub, predictors + [TARGET])
257 |     X = pd.DataFrame(
258 |         {col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in predictors}
259 |     )
260 |     y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce")
261 |     return X, y

264 | def ridge_train_test(
265 |     df: pd.DataFrame,
266 |     predictors: list[str],
267 |     train_years: tuple[int, ...] = (2022, 2023, 2024),
268 |     test_year: int = 2025,
269 |     alpha: float | None = None,
270 | ) -> dict:
271 |     """Fit a ridge regression on ``train_years`` and predict ``test_year``.
272 | 
273 |     The scaler and the regularisation strength (cross-validated via ``RidgeCV``
274 |     when ``alpha`` is ``None``) are determined from the training data only, then
275 |     applied unchanged to the held-out year, so the test-year metrics are
276 |     genuinely out of sample. Returns training/test sizes, the selected alpha,
277 |     in-sample (train) R², out-of-sample (test) R², RMSE and MAE, the fitted
278 |     coefficients, and the test-year observed and predicted values.
279 |     """
280 |     X_train, y_train = _prepare_xy(df, predictors, list(train_years))
281 |     X_test, y_test = _prepare_xy(df, predictors, [test_year])
282 | 
283 |     scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_train)
284 |     X_train_std = scaler.transform(X_train)
285 |     X_test_std = scaler.transform(X_test)
286 | 
287 |     if alpha is None:
288 |         model = RidgeCV(alphas=RIDGE_ALPHAS).fit(X_train_std, y_train)
289 |     else:
290 |         model = Ridge(alpha=alpha).fit(X_train_std, y_train)
291 | 
292 |     y_pred = model.predict(X_test_std)
293 | 
294 |     ss_res = float(((y_test - y_pred) ** 2).sum())
295 |     ss_tot = float(((y_test - y_test.mean()) ** 2).sum())
296 |     r2_test = 1 - ss_res / ss_tot
297 |     rmse = float(np.sqrt(((y_test.to_numpy() - y_pred) ** 2).mean()))
298 |     mae = float(np.abs(y_test.to_numpy() - y_pred).mean())
299 | 
300 |     coefs = pd.DataFrame(
301 |         [{"Term": "Intercept", "Coefficient": float(model.intercept_)}]
302 |         + [
303 |             {"Term": col, "Coefficient": float(coef)}
304 |             for col, coef in zip(predictors, model.coef_)
305 |         ]
306 |     )
307 | 
308 |     return {
309 |         "n_train": int(len(X_train)),
310 |         "n_test": int(len(X_test)),
311 |         "alpha": float(model.alpha_) if alpha is None else float(alpha),
312 |         "r2_train": float(model.score(X_train_std, y_train)),
313 |         "r2_test": float(r2_test),
314 |         "rmse": rmse,
315 |         "mae": mae,
316 |         "coefs": coefs,
317 |         "y_test": y_test.to_numpy(),
318 |         "y_pred": y_pred,
319 |     }

def _applicable_mask(df: pd.DataFrame, columns: list[str]) -> pd.Series:
    """Rows where every conditional column is applicable (not the NA marker)."""
    mask = pd.Series(True, index=df.index)
    for column in columns:
        if column in data_utilities.CONDITIONAL_COLUMNS:
            mask &= ~df[column].eq(data_utilities.NA_MARKER).fillna(False)
    return mask


def linear_model(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    predictors: list[str],
    complete_on: list[str] | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Fit a linear regression of the target on ``predictors``.

    Restricted to launched concepts (the target is launch-phase only), to rows
    where the ``complete_on`` columns are applicable, and to per-model complete
    cases on ``complete_on`` and the target. ``complete_on`` defaults to
    ``predictors``; pass it explicitly to refit a model on a fixed subset.
    """
    if complete_on is None:
        complete_on = predictors
    launched = df[df["Launched"] == 1]
    launched = launched[_applicable_mask(launched, complete_on)]
    sub = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(launched, complete_on + [TARGET])

    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in predictors}
    )
    y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce")

    model = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)
    n = len(X)
    k = len(predictors)
    r2 = float(model.score(X, y))
    adj_r2 = 1 - (1 - r2) * (n - 1) / (n - k - 1)

    coefs = pd.DataFrame(
        [{"Term": "Intercept", "Coefficient": float(model.intercept_)}]
        + [
            {"Term": col, "Coefficient": float(coef)}
            for col, coef in zip(predictors, model.coef_)
        ]
    )

    return {
        "n": n,
        "r2": r2,
        "adj_r2": adj_r2,
        "coefs": coefs,
        "coef": dict(zip(predictors, model.coef_.tolist())),
        "y": y.to_numpy(),
        "y_pred": model.predict(X),
    }


def ridge_model(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    predictors: list[str],
    complete_on: list[str] | None = None,
    alpha: float | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Fit a ridge regression of the target on ``predictors``.

    Predictors are standardised to z-scores so the L2 penalty treats each
    variable equally. When ``alpha`` is ``None`` (default) the regularisation
    strength is selected by leave-one-out cross-validation (``RidgeCV``);
    otherwise a fixed ``alpha`` is used. Passing ``alpha=0.0`` recovers an
    unregularised OLS fit on the standardised predictors, giving per-SD
    coefficients directly comparable with the ridge ones. The sample is
    restricted exactly like :func:`linear_model`.
    """
    if complete_on is None:
        complete_on = predictors
    launched = df[df["Launched"] == 1]
    launched = launched[_applicable_mask(launched, complete_on)]
    sub = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(launched, complete_on + [TARGET])

    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in predictors}
    )
    y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce")

    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X)
    X_std = pd.DataFrame(scaler.transform(X), columns=predictors)

    if alpha is None:
        model = RidgeCV(alphas=RIDGE_ALPHAS).fit(X_std, y)
    else:
        model = Ridge(alpha=alpha).fit(X_std, y)
    n = len(X)
    r2 = float(model.score(X_std, y))

    coefs = pd.DataFrame(
        [{"Term": "Intercept", "Coefficient": float(model.intercept_)}]
        + [
            {"Term": col, "Coefficient": float(coef)}
            for col, coef in zip(predictors, model.coef_)
        ]
    )

    return {
        "n": n,
        "r2": r2,
        "alpha": float(model.alpha_) if alpha is None else float(alpha),
        "coefs": coefs,
        "coef": dict(zip(predictors, model.coef_.tolist())),
        "y": y.to_numpy(),
        "y_pred": model.predict(X_std),
    }


def _prepare_xy(
    df: pd.DataFrame, predictors: list[str], years: list[int]
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
    """Restrict to launched concepts in ``years`` with applicable + complete data.

    Returns the numeric predictor matrix ``X`` and target ``y``. Structural
    ``"NA"`` markers are excluded via the applicability mask, then genuinely
    missing values (``pd.NA``) are dropped per-model on the predictors and the
    target.
    """
    sub = df[(df["Test_Year"].isin(years)) & (df["Launched"] == 1)]
    sub = sub[_applicable_mask(sub, predictors)]
    sub = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(sub, predictors + [TARGET])
    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in predictors}
    )
    y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce")
    return X, y


def ridge_train_test(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    predictors: list[str],
    train_years: tuple[int, ...] = (2022, 2023, 2024),
    test_year: int = 2025,
    alpha: float | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Fit a ridge regression on ``train_years`` and predict ``test_year``.

    The scaler and the regularisation strength (cross-validated via ``RidgeCV``
    when ``alpha`` is ``None``) are determined from the training data only, then
    applied unchanged to the held-out year, so the test-year metrics are
    genuinely out of sample. Returns training/test sizes, the selected alpha,
    in-sample (train) RÂ², out-of-sample (test) RÂ², RMSE and MAE, the fitted
    coefficients, and the test-year observed and predicted values.
    """
    X_train, y_train = _prepare_xy(df, predictors, list(train_years))
    X_test, y_test = _prepare_xy(df, predictors, [test_year])

    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_train)
    X_train_std = scaler.transform(X_train)
    X_test_std = scaler.transform(X_test)

    if alpha is None:
        model = RidgeCV(alphas=RIDGE_ALPHAS).fit(X_train_std, y_train)
    else:
        model = Ridge(alpha=alpha).fit(X_train_std, y_train)

    y_pred = model.predict(X_test_std)

    ss_res = float(((y_test - y_pred) ** 2).sum())
    ss_tot = float(((y_test - y_test.mean()) ** 2).sum())
    r2_test = 1 - ss_res / ss_tot
    rmse = float(np.sqrt(((y_test.to_numpy() - y_pred) ** 2).mean()))
    mae = float(np.abs(y_test.to_numpy() - y_pred).mean())

    coefs = pd.DataFrame(
        [{"Term": "Intercept", "Coefficient": float(model.intercept_)}]
        + [
            {"Term": col, "Coefficient": float(coef)}
            for col, coef in zip(predictors, model.coef_)
        ]
    )

    return {
        "n_train": int(len(X_train)),
        "n_test": int(len(X_test)),
        "alpha": float(model.alpha_) if alpha is None else float(alpha),
        "r2_train": float(model.score(X_train_std, y_train)),
        "r2_test": float(r2_test),
        "rmse": rmse,
        "mae": mae,
        "coefs": coefs,
        "y_test": y_test.to_numpy(),
        "y_pred": y_pred,
    }

def ridge_model(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    predictors: list[str],
    complete_on: list[str] | None = None,
    alpha: float | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Fit a ridge regression of the target on ``predictors``.

    Predictors are standardised to z-scores so the L2 penalty treats each
    variable equally. When ``alpha`` is ``None`` (default) the regularisation
    strength is selected by leave-one-out cross-validation (``RidgeCV``);
    otherwise a fixed ``alpha`` is used. Passing ``alpha=0.0`` recovers an
    unregularised OLS fit on the standardised predictors, giving per-SD
    coefficients directly comparable with the ridge ones. The sample is
    restricted exactly like :func:`linear_model`.
    """
    if complete_on is None:
        complete_on = predictors
    launched = df[df["Launched"] == 1]
    launched = launched[_applicable_mask(launched, complete_on)]
    sub = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(launched, complete_on + [TARGET])

    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in predictors}
    )
    y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce")

    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X)
    X_std = pd.DataFrame(scaler.transform(X), columns=predictors)

    if alpha is None:
        model = RidgeCV(alphas=RIDGE_ALPHAS).fit(X_std, y)
    else:
        model = Ridge(alpha=alpha).fit(X_std, y)
    n = len(X)
    r2 = float(model.score(X_std, y))

    coefs = pd.DataFrame(
        [{"Term": "Intercept", "Coefficient": float(model.intercept_)}]
        + [
            {"Term": col, "Coefficient": float(coef)}
            for col, coef in zip(predictors, model.coef_)
        ]
    )

    return {
        "n": n,
        "r2": r2,
        "alpha": float(model.alpha_) if alpha is None else float(alpha),
        "coefs": coefs,
        "coef": dict(zip(predictors, model.coef_.tolist())),
        "y": y.to_numpy(),
        "y_pred": model.predict(X_std),
    }


def _prepare_xy(
    df: pd.DataFrame, predictors: list[str], years: list[int]
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
    """Restrict to launched concepts in ``years`` with applicable + complete data.

    Returns the numeric predictor matrix ``X`` and target ``y``. Structural
    ``"NA"`` markers are excluded via the applicability mask, then genuinely
    missing values (``pd.NA``) are dropped per-model on the predictors and the
    target.
    """
    sub = df[(df["Test_Year"].isin(years)) & (df["Launched"] == 1)]
    sub = sub[_applicable_mask(sub, predictors)]
    sub = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(sub, predictors + [TARGET])
    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in predictors}
    )
    y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce")
    return X, y

```python
def repeated_kfold_compare(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    alpha: float | None = None,
    n_splits: int = 7,
    n_repeats: int = 20,
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> dict:
    sub = _shared_implicit_subset(df)
    X_full = pd.DataFrame({col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS})
    y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce").to_numpy()

    rkf = RepeatedKFold(n_splits=n_splits, n_repeats=n_repeats, random_state=random_state)

    rows = []
    for train_idx, test_idx in rkf.split(X_full):
        X_tr = X_full.iloc[train_idx]
        X_te = X_full.iloc[test_idx]
        y_tr, y_te = y[train_idx], y[test_idx]

        beh = _fold_metrics(X_tr, y_tr, X_te, y_te, BEHAVIOURAL_CV_PREDICTORS, alpha)
        imp = _fold_metrics(X_tr, y_tr, X_te, y_te, IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS, alpha)
        rows.append({
            "r2_diff": imp["r2"] - beh["r2"],
            "rmse_diff": imp["rmse"] - beh["rmse"],
            "mae_diff": imp["mae"] - beh["mae"],
            "r2_behavioural": beh["r2"],
            "r2_implicit": imp["r2"],
        })

    res = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return {
        "n_cases": int(len(sub)),
        "n_splits": n_splits,
        "n_repeats": n_repeats,
        "n_folds": len(res),
        "alpha": None if alpha is None else float(alpha),
        "r2_diff": res["r2_diff"].to_numpy(),
        "rmse_diff": res["rmse_diff"].to_numpy(),
        "mae_diff": res["mae_diff"].to_numpy(),
        "r2_behavioural": res["r2_behavioural"].to_numpy(),
        "r2_implicit": res["r2_implicit"].to_numpy(),
    }
```

```python
def _fold_metrics(X_tr, y_tr, X_te, y_te, predictors, alpha):
    X_tr = X_tr[predictors]
    X_te = X_te[predictors]
    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_tr)
    Xtr = scaler.transform(X_tr)
    Xte = scaler.transform(X_te)
    if alpha is None:
        model = RidgeCV(alphas=RIDGE_ALPHAS).fit(Xtr, y_tr)
    else:
        model = Ridge(alpha=alpha).fit(Xtr, y_tr)
    y_pred = model.predict(Xte)
    ss_res = float(((y_te - y_pred) ** 2).sum())
    ss_tot = float(((y_te - y_te.mean()) ** 2).sum())
    r2 = 1 - ss_res / ss_tot
    rmse = float(np.sqrt(((y_te - y_pred) ** 2).mean()))
    mae = float(np.abs(y_te - y_pred).mean())
    return {"r2": r2, "rmse": rmse, "mae": mae}
```

```python
def _shared_implicit_subset(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The shared cases used by both CV models (implicit subsample)."""
    predictors = IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS
    launched = df[df["Launched"] == 1]
    launched = launched[_applicable_mask(launched, predictors)]
    return data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(launched, predictors + [TARGET])


def _fold_metrics(
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: np.ndarray,
    X_test: pd.DataFrame,
    y_test: np.ndarray,
    predictors: list[str],
    alpha: float | None,
) -> dict:
    """Fit a ridge model on one CV fold and score it on the held-out fold.

    ``alpha`` is fixed, or selected by leave-one-out ``RidgeCV`` when ``None``.
    Returns out-of-sample R², RMSE and MAE (implicit − behavioural handled by
    the caller). The scaler is fit on the training fold only.
    """
    Xtr = X_train[predictors]
    Xte = X_test[predictors]
    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(Xtr)
    Xtr_std = scaler.transform(Xtr)
    Xte_std = scaler.transform(Xte)

    if alpha is None:
        model = RidgeCV(alphas=RIDGE_ALPHAS).fit(Xtr_std, y_train)
    else:
        model = Ridge(alpha=alpha).fit(Xtr_std, y_train)

    y_pred = model.predict(Xte_std)
    ss_res = float(((y_test - y_pred) ** 2).sum())
    ss_tot = float(((y_test - y_test.mean()) ** 2).sum())
    r2 = 1 - ss_res / ss_tot
    rmse = float(np.sqrt(((y_test - y_pred) ** 2).mean()))
    mae = float(np.abs(y_test - y_pred).mean())
    return {"r2": r2, "rmse": rmse, "mae": mae}


def repeated_kfold_compare(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    alpha: float | None = None,
    n_splits: int = 7,
    n_repeats: int = 20,
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> dict:
    """Repeated K-fold comparison of the implicit vs behavioural ridge models.

    Both models are fit on identical folds and identical cases (the shared
    implicit subsample), so within-fold differences isolate the contribution of
    ``Implicit_Score``. ``alpha`` fixed (option A) or per-fold ``RidgeCV``
    (option B, ``alpha=None``). Returns fold-level differences (implicit −
    behavioural) in R², RMSE and MAE, plus the per-fold R² of each model.
    """
    sub = _shared_implicit_subset(df)
    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS}
    )
    y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce").to_numpy()

    rkf = RepeatedKFold(n_splits=n_splits, n_repeats=n_repeats, random_state=random_state)

    r2_diff, rmse_diff, mae_diff = [], [], []
    r2_behavioural, r2_implicit = [], []
    for train_idx, test_idx in rkf.split(X):
        beh = _fold_metrics(
            X.iloc[train_idx], y[train_idx], X.iloc[test_idx], y[test_idx],
            BEHAVIOURAL_CV_PREDICTORS, alpha,
        )
        imp = _fold_metrics(
            X.iloc[train_idx], y[train_idx], X.iloc[test_idx], y[test_idx],
            IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS, alpha,
        )
        r2_diff.append(imp["r2"] - beh["r2"])
        rmse_diff.append(imp["rmse"] - beh["rmse"])
        mae_diff.append(imp["mae"] - beh["mae"])
        r2_behavioural.append(beh["r2"])
        r2_implicit.append(imp["r2"])

    return {
        "n_cases": int(len(sub)),
        "n_splits": n_splits,
        "n_repeats": n_repeats,
        "n_folds": n_splits * n_repeats,
        "alpha": None if alpha is None else float(alpha),
        "r2_diff": np.asarray(r2_diff),
        "rmse_diff": np.asarray(rmse_diff),
        "mae_diff": np.asarray(mae_diff),
        "r2_behavioural": np.asarray(r2_behavioural),
        "r2_implicit": np.asarray(r2_implicit),
    }


def summarise_fold_diffs(diffs: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    """Summarise an array of fold differences (implicit − behavioural).

    Returns the mean, standard deviation, median, 2.5th/97.5th-percentile
    confidence interval, and the proportion of folds where the difference is
    positive (implicit better for R²; negate for RMSE/MAE).
    """
    diffs = np.asarray(diffs)
    ci_lo, ci_hi = np.percentile(diffs, [2.5, 97.5])
    return {
        "mean": float(diffs.mean()),
        "sd": float(diffs.std()),
        "median": float(np.median(diffs)),
        "ci_lo": float(ci_lo),
        "ci_hi": float(ci_hi),
        "p_positive": float((diffs > 0).mean()),
    }
```

```python
def diff_summary_table(res: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build the metric summary table for a repeated-K-fold result."""
    rows = []
    for metric, key, lower_is_better in [
        ("Δ R²", "r2_diff", False),
        ("Δ RMSE", "rmse_diff", True),
        ("Δ MAE", "mae_diff", True),
    ]:
        s = summarise_fold_diffs(res[key])
        better = s["p_positive"] if not lower_is_better else 1 - s["p_positive"]
        rows.append({
            "Metric": metric,
            "Mean": f"{s['mean']:+.3f}",
            "SD": f"{s['sd']:.3f}",
            "Median": f"{s['median']:+.3f}",
            "95% CI": f"[{s['ci_lo']:+.3f}, {s['ci_hi']:+.3f}]",
            "Implicit better (% of folds)": f"{better * 100:.0f}",
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
```

## 11. Repeated K-fold CV â€” isolating the implicit measure's contribution
A single 2025 hold-out (23 concepts) cannot tell whether the implicit model's failure reflects a hard fold or too few points. Repeated K-fold cross-validation replaces that one split with many random splits of the shared 70-case implicit subsample. On every fold the behavioural and implicit models are fit on the *same* training cases and evaluated on the *same* test cases, and the within-fold difference (implicit âˆ’ behavioural) is recorded. Because the folds are paired, any overall difficulty of a fold cancels out, and the distribution of differences isolates what ``Implicit_Score`` adds. Two regularisation strategies are compared: a fixed Î± (option A), so the only difference between the models is the predictor set, and a per-fold cross-validated Î± (option B), which pits the best-tuned implicit model against the best-tuned behavioural model.

Both models share the same fixed Î± = 10, so the only difference between them is the predictor set. Over 140 folds the behavioural model's fold RÂ² averages -0.145 and the implicit model's -0.095; a positive Î” means the implicit model is the better of the two on that fold.

```python
def _shared_subset(df: pd.DataFrame, predictors: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cases complete on ``predictors`` and the target, applicable for all of them.

    Used so both models in a pairwise CV comparison are fit on identical cases.
    """
    launched = df[df["Launched"] == 1]
    launched = launched[_applicable_mask(launched, predictors)]
    return data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(launched, predictors + [TARGET])


def repeated_kfold_compare(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    base_predictors: list[str],
    full_predictors: list[str],
    alpha: float | None = None,
    n_splits: int = 7,
    n_repeats: int = 20,
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> dict:
    """Repeated K-fold comparison of two nested ridge models.

    The base model uses ``base_predictors``; the full model uses
    ``full_predictors`` (a superset). Both are fit on identical folds of the
    shared subset (cases complete on ``full_predictors``), so within-fold
    differences isolate the contribution of the added predictors. With ``alpha``
    fixed (option A) the two models differ only in their predictor set; with
    ``alpha=None`` (option B) each model selects its own strength by
    leave-one-out ``RidgeCV``. Returns fold-level differences (full − base) in
    R², RMSE and MAE, plus each model's per-fold R².
    """
    sub = _shared_subset(df, full_predictors)
    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce")
            for col in full_predictors
        }
    )
    y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce").to_numpy()

    rkf = RepeatedKFold(
        n_splits=n_splits, n_repeats=n_repeats, random_state=random_state
    )

    r2_diff, rmse_diff, mae_diff = [], [], []
    r2_base, r2_full = [], []
    for train_idx, test_idx in rkf.split(X):
        base = _fold_metrics(
            X.iloc[train_idx],
            y[train_idx],
            X.iloc[test_idx],
            y[test_idx],
            base_predictors,
            alpha,
        )
        full = _fold_metrics(
            X.iloc[train_idx],
            y[train_idx],
            X.iloc[test_idx],
            y[test_idx],
            full_predictors,
            alpha,
        )
        r2_diff.append(full["r2"] - base["r2"])
        rmse_diff.append(full["rmse"] - base["rmse"])
        mae_diff.append(full["mae"] - base["mae"])
        r2_base.append(base["r2"])
        r2_full.append(full["r2"])

    return {
        "n_cases": int(len(sub)),
        "n_splits": n_splits,
        "n_repeats": n_repeats,
        "n_folds": n_splits * n_repeats,
        "alpha": None if alpha is None else float(alpha),
        "r2_diff": np.asarray(r2_diff),
        "rmse_diff": np.asarray(rmse_diff),
        "mae_diff": np.asarray(mae_diff),
        "r2_base": np.asarray(r2_base),
        "r2_full": np.asarray(r2_full),
    }
```

def _shared_implicit_subset(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The shared cases used by both CV models (the implicit subsample)."""
    predictors = IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS
    launched = df[df["Launched"] == 1]
    launched = launched[_applicable_mask(launched, predictors)]
    return data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(launched, predictors + [TARGET])


def _fold_metrics(
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: np.ndarray,
    X_test: pd.DataFrame,
    y_test: np.ndarray,
    predictors: list[str],
    alpha: float | None,
) -> dict:
    """Fit a ridge model on one CV fold and score it on the held-out fold.

    ``alpha`` is used directly, or selected by leave-one-out ``RidgeCV`` when
    ``None``. The scaler is fit on the training fold only. Returns out-of-sample
    RÂ², RMSE and MAE.
    """
    Xtr = X_train[predictors]
    Xte = X_test[predictors]
    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(Xtr)
    Xtr_std = scaler.transform(Xtr)
    Xte_std = scaler.transform(Xte)

    if alpha is None:
        model = RidgeCV(alphas=RIDGE_ALPHAS).fit(Xtr_std, y_train)
    else:
        model = Ridge(alpha=alpha).fit(Xtr_std, y_train)

    y_pred = model.predict(Xte_std)
    ss_res = float(((y_test - y_pred) ** 2).sum())
    ss_tot = float(((y_test - y_test.mean()) ** 2).sum())
    r2 = 1 - ss_res / ss_tot
    rmse = float(np.sqrt(((y_test - y_pred) ** 2).mean()))
    mae = float(np.abs(y_test - y_pred).mean())
    return {"r2": r2, "rmse": rmse, "mae": mae}


def repeated_kfold_compare(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    alpha: float | None = None,
    n_splits: int = 7,
    n_repeats: int = 20,
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> dict:
    """Repeated K-fold comparison of the implicit vs behavioural ridge models.

    Both models are fit on identical folds and identical cases (the shared
    implicit subsample), so within-fold differences isolate the contribution of
    ``Implicit_Score``. With ``alpha`` fixed (option A) the two models differ
    only in their predictor set; with ``alpha=None`` (option B) each model
    selects its own strength by leave-one-out ``RidgeCV``. Returns fold-level
    differences (implicit âˆ’ behavioural) in RÂ², RMSE and MAE, plus each model's
    per-fold RÂ².
    """
    sub = _shared_implicit_subset(df)
    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce")
            for col in IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS
        }
    )
    y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce").to_numpy()

    rkf = RepeatedKFold(
        n_splits=n_splits, n_repeats=n_repeats, random_state=random_state
    )

    r2_diff, rmse_diff, mae_diff = [], [], []
    r2_behavioural, r2_implicit = [], []
    for train_idx, test_idx in rkf.split(X):
        beh = _fold_metrics(
            X.iloc[train_idx],
            y[train_idx],
            X.iloc[test_idx],
            y[test_idx],
            BEHAVIOURAL_CV_PREDICTORS,
            alpha,
        )
        imp = _fold_metrics(
            X.iloc[train_idx],
            y[train_idx],
            X.iloc[test_idx],
            y[test_idx],
            IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS,
            alpha,
        )
        r2_diff.append(imp["r2"] - beh["r2"])
        rmse_diff.append(imp["rmse"] - beh["rmse"])
        mae_diff.append(imp["mae"] - beh["mae"])
        r2_behavioural.append(beh["r2"])
        r2_implicit.append(imp["r2"])

    return {
        "n_cases": int(len(sub)),
        "n_splits": n_splits,
        "n_repeats": n_repeats,
        "n_folds": n_splits * n_repeats,
        "alpha": None if alpha is None else float(alpha),
        "r2_diff": np.asarray(r2_diff),
        "rmse_diff": np.asarray(rmse_diff),
        "mae_diff": np.asarray(mae_diff),
        "r2_behavioural": np.asarray(r2_behavioural),
        "r2_implicit": np.asarray(r2_implicit),
    }


def summarise_fold_diffs(diffs: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    """Summarise an array of fold differences (implicit âˆ’ behavioural).

    Returns the mean, standard deviation, median, 2.5th/97.5th-percentile
    confidence interval, and the proportion of folds where the difference is
    positive (implicit better for RÂ²; subtract from one for RMSE/MAE).
    """
    diffs = np.asarray(diffs)
    ci_lo, ci_hi = np.percentile(diffs, [2.5, 97.5])
    return {
        "mean": float(diffs.mean()),
        "sd": float(diffs.std()),
        "median": float(np.median(diffs)),
        "ci_lo": float(ci_lo),
        "ci_hi": float(ci_hi),
        "p_positive": float((diffs > 0).mean()),
    }


def diff_summary_table(res: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Build the metric summary table for a repeated-K-fold result."""
    rows = []
    for metric, key, lower_is_better in [
        ("Î” RÂ²", "r2_diff", False),
        ("Î” RMSE", "rmse_diff", True),
        ("Î” MAE", "mae_diff", True),
    ]:
        s = summarise_fold_diffs(res[key])
        better = s["p_positive"] if not lower_is_better else 1 - s["p_positive"]
        rows.append(
            {
                "Metric": metric,
                "Mean": f"{s['mean']:+.3f}",
                "SD": f"{s['sd']:.3f}",
                "Median": f"{s['median']:+.3f}",
                "95% CI": f"[{s['ci_lo']:+.3f}, {s['ci_hi']:+.3f}]",
                "Implicit better (% of folds)": f"{better * 100:.0f}",
            }
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

```
def repeated_kfold_compare(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
```
```
    base_predictors: list[str],
    full_predictors: list[str],
    alpha: float | None = None,
    n_splits: int = 7,
    n_repeats: int = 20,
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> dict:
    """Repeated K-fold comparison of two nested ridge models.

    The base model uses ``base_predictors`` and the full model uses
    ``full_predictors`` (a superset). Both are fit on identical folds of the
    shared subset (cases complete on ``full_predictors``), so within-fold
    differences isolate the contribution of the added predictors. With ``alpha``
    fixed (option A) the two models differ only in their predictor set; with
    ``alpha=None`` (option B) each model selects its own strength by
    leave-one-out ``RidgeCV``. Returns fold-level differences (full − base) in
    R², RMSE and MAE, plus each model's per-fold R².
    """
    sub = _shared_subset(df, full_predictors)
    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce")
            for col in full_predictors
        }
    )
    y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce").to_numpy()

    rkf = RepeatedKFold(
        n_splits=n_splits, n_repeats=n_repeats, random_state=random_state
    )

    r2_diff, rmse_diff, mae_diff = [], [], []
    r2_base, r2_full = [], []
    for train_idx, test_idx in rkf.split(X):
        base = _fold_metrics(
            X.iloc[train_idx],
            y[train_idx],
            X.iloc[test_idx],
            y[test_idx],
            base_predictors,
            alpha,
        )
        full = _fold_metrics(
            X.iloc[train_idx],
            y[train_idx],
            X.iloc[test_idx],
            y[test_idx],
            full_predictors,
            alpha,
        )
        r2_diff.append(full["r2"] - base["r2"])
        rmse_diff.append(full["rmse"] - base["rmse"])
        mae_diff.append(full["mae"] - base["mae"])
        r2_base.append(base["r2"])
        r2_full.append(full["r2"])

    return {
        "n_cases": int(len(sub)),
        "n_splits": n_splits,
        "n_repeats": n_repeats,
        "n_folds": n_splits * n_repeats,
        "alpha": None if alpha is None else float(alpha),
        "r2_diff": np.asarray(r2_diff),
        "rmse_diff": np.asarray(rmse_diff),
        "mae_diff": np.asarray(mae_diff),
        "r2_base": np.asarray(r2_base),
        "r2_full": np.asarray(r2_full),
    }
```

"""Predictive modelling of launch outcomes from concept-test research.

Defines the modelling target â€” a binary success outcome derived from
``Sales_vs_Target_Pct`` â€” compares success between research packages, fits a
first linear model, and records the caveats that bound interpretation. Writes to
``output/logs/modelling.md``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression, Ridge, RidgeCV
from sklearn.model_selection import RepeatedKFold
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

import data_utilities
import log_writer

#: Success threshold: ``Sales_vs_Target_Pct`` >= this value is a success.
SUCCESS_THRESHOLD: float = 100.0

#: Survey (stated) measures used as predictors in the first model.
SURVEY_MEASURES: list[str] = ["Stated_Appeal", "Purchase_Intent"]

#: Behavioural measure added as a predictor in the second model.
BEHAVIOURAL_MEASURES: list[str] = ["Behavioural_Choice_Pct"]

#: Implicit measure added as a predictor in the third model.
IMPLICIT_MEASURES: list[str] = ["Implicit_Score"]

#: Regression target for the first model.
TARGET: str = "Sales_vs_Target_Pct"

#: Regularisation strengths tried by cross-validation for the ridge models.
RIDGE_ALPHAS: list[float] = [0.1, 1.0, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 50.0, 100.0, 200.0]

#: Predictor sets for the behavioural and implicit models compared in the
#: repeated K-fold CV. Both are restricted to the shared implicit subsample so
#: the only difference between them is the predictor set.
BEHAVIOURAL_CV_PREDICTORS: list[str] = SURVEY_MEASURES + BEHAVIOURAL_MEASURES
IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS: list[str] = BEHAVIOURAL_CV_PREDICTORS + IMPLICIT_MEASURES

#: Fixed regularisation strength used by the "clean" comparison (option A),
#: where the two models differ only in their predictor set.
FIXED_ALPHA: float = 10.0

#: Regularisation strengths used to check option A's sensitivity to alpha.
ALPHA_SENSITIVITY: list[float] = [0.0, 10.0, 50.0]


def _context_facts(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[str, float | int]:
    """Compute the small set of data facts referenced by the caveats."""
    # Implicit_Score subsample (Combined packages only).
    implicit = df[df["Research_Package"] == "Combined"]
    implicit_complete = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(implicit, ["Implicit_Score"])

    # Collinearity between the research-economics metrics.
    cost_days = df[["Research_Cost_EUR", "Turnaround_Days"]].apply(
        pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce"
    )

    # Package-mix shift 2022 -> 2025.
    package_pct = (
        pd.crosstab(df["Test_Year"], df["Research_Package"])
        .div(pd.crosstab(df["Test_Year"], df["Research_Package"]).sum(axis=1), axis=0)
        * 100
    )

    return {
        "n_implicit_applicable": len(implicit),
        "n_implicit_complete": len(implicit_complete),
        "implicit_missing_rate": (len(implicit) - len(implicit_complete))
        / len(implicit)
        * 100,
        "r_cost_days": float(cost_days.corr().iloc[0, 1]),
        "survey_2022": package_pct.loc[2022, "Survey"],
        "survey_2025": package_pct.loc[2025, "Survey"],
    }


def _package_success(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """Compare binary success across research packages (Survey baseline).

    Restricted to launched concepts with an observed ``Sales_vs_Target_Pct``.
    """
    launched = df[df["Launched"] == 1].copy()
    launched["sales"] = pd.to_numeric(launched["Sales_vs_Target_Pct"], errors="coerce")
    sub = launched[launched["sales"].notna()].copy()
    sub["success"] = (sub["sales"] >= SUCCESS_THRESHOLD).astype(int)

    ct = pd.crosstab(sub["Research_Package"], sub["success"])
    chi2, p, dof, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(ct)

    success_rate = ct[1] / ct.sum(axis=1) * 100
    n = ct.sum(axis=1)

    cost = launched.groupby("Research_Package", observed=True)["Research_Cost_EUR"].apply(
        lambda s: pd.to_numeric(s, errors="coerce").mean()
    )
    days = launched.groupby("Research_Package", observed=True)["Turnaround_Days"].apply(
        lambda s: pd.to_numeric(s, errors="coerce").mean()
    )

    base_success = success_rate["Survey"]
    base_cost = cost["Survey"]
    base_days = days["Survey"]

    def table_pair(
        self,
        left: Any,
        right: Any,
        left_headers: Sequence[Any] | None = None,
        right_headers: Sequence[Any] | None = None,
        *,
        float_format: Any = None,
        na_rep: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        """Render two tables side by side, separated by an empty column.

        ``left`` and ``right`` may be any form accepted by :meth:`table` (a
        DataFrame, a columnar dict, or an iterable of rows). The shorter table
        is padded with empty cells so its rows align with the longer one.
        """
        left_rows, left_headers = _coerce_table(left, left_headers)
        right_rows, right_headers = _coerce_table(right, right_headers)

        width_left = len(left_headers) if left_headers else 0
        width_right = len(right_headers) if right_headers else 0
        for row in left_rows:
            width_left = max(width_left, len(row))
        for row in right_rows:
            width_right = max(width_right, len(row))
        if width_left == 0 and width_right == 0:
            return

        left_headers = list(left_headers or [])
        right_headers = list(right_headers or [])
        left_headers += [""] * (width_left - len(left_headers))
        right_headers += [""] * (width_right - len(right_headers))

        n_rows = max(len(left_rows), len(right_rows))

        def padded(rows: list[tuple], width: int) -> list[list]:
            out = [list(row) + [""] * (width - len(row)) for row in rows]
            out += [[""] * width] * (n_rows - len(out))
            return out

        left_rows = padded(left_rows, width_left)
        right_rows = padded(right_rows, width_right)

        def fmt(value: Any) -> str:
            return _format_cell(value, float_format, na_rep)

        total_width = width_left + 1 + width_right
        lines = [
            "| "
            + " | ".join(fmt(c) for c in left_headers + [""] + right_headers)
            + " |",
            "| " + " | ".join("---" for _ in range(total_width)) + " |",
        ]
        for lrow, rrow in zip(left_rows, right_rows):
            lines.append(
                "| " + " | ".join(fmt(c) for c in lrow + [""] + rrow) + " |"
            )

        self.write("\n".join(lines))
        self.blank()

```python
def logistic_model(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    predictors: list[str],
    complete_on: list[str] | None = None,
    C: float = LOGISTIC_C,
) -> dict:
    """Fit a regularised logistic regression predicting binary success.

    Success is ``Sales_vs_Target_Pct >= SUCCESS_THRESHOLD``. The model uses an
    L2 penalty with balanced class weights (``LogisticRegression``), predictors
    standardised to z-scores, and ``C`` as the inverse regularisation strength.
    The sample is restricted exactly like :func:`linear_model`. Returns
    coefficients (log-odds and odds ratios) and in-sample classification
    metrics.
    """
    if complete_on is None:
        complete_on = predictors
    launched = df[df["Launched"] == 1]
    launched = launched[_applicable_mask(launched, complete_on)]
    sub = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(launched, complete_on + [TARGET])

    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in predictors}
    )
    y_raw = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce")
    y = (y_raw >= SUCCESS_THRESHOLD).astype(int)

    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X)
    X_std = pd.DataFrame(scaler.transform(X), columns=predictors)

    model = LogisticRegression(
        penalty="l2", C=C, class_weight="balanced", solver="lbfgs", max_iter=2000
    ).fit(X_std, y)

    y_prob = model.predict_proba(X_std)[:, 1]
    y_pred = model.predict(X_std)

    coefs = pd.DataFrame(
        [{"Term": "Intercept", "Coefficient": float(model.intercept_[0]), "Odds ratio": float(np.exp(model.intercept_[0]))}]
        + [
            {"Term": col, "Coefficient": float(coef), "Odds ratio": float(np.exp(coef))}
            for col, coef in zip(predictors, model.coef_[0])
        ]
    )

    return {
        "n": len(X),
        "success_rate": float(y.mean() * 100),
        "coefs": coefs,
        "accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y, y_pred)),
        "balanced_accuracy": float(balanced_accuracy_score(y, y_pred)),
        "precision": float(precision_score(y, y_pred, zero_division=0)),
        "recall": float(recall_score(y, y_pred, zero_division=0)),
        "f1": float(f1_score(y, y_pred, zero_division=0)),
        "roc_auc": float(roc_auc_score(y, y_prob)),
    }
```

    y = (y_raw >= SUCCESS_THRESHOLD).astype(int)

    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X)
    X_std = pd.DataFrame(scaler.transform(X), columns=predictors)

    model = LogisticRegression(
        penalty="l2", C=C, class_weight="balanced", solver="lbfgs", max_iter=2000
    ).fit(X_std, y)

                "Coefficient": float(coef),
                "Odds ratio": float(np.exp(coef)),
            }
            for col, coef in zip(predictors, model.coef_[0])
        ]
    )

    return {

def _prepare_xy(
    df: pd.DataFrame, predictors: list[str], years: list[int]
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
    """Restrict to launched concepts in ``years`` with applicable + complete data.

    Returns the numeric predictor matrix ``X`` and target ``y``. Structural
    ``"NA"`` markers are excluded via the applicability mask, then genuinely
    missing values (``pd.NA``) are dropped per-model on the predictors and the
    target.
    """
    sub = df[(df["Test_Year"].isin(years)) & (df["Launched"] == 1)]
    sub = sub[_applicable_mask(sub, predictors)]
    sub = data_utilities.drop_missing_rows(sub, predictors + [TARGET])
    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce") for col in predictors}
    )
    y = pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce")
    return X, y


def ridge_train_test(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    predictors: list[str],
    train_years: tuple[int, ...] = (2022, 2023, 2024),
    test_year: int = 2025,
    alpha: float | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Fit a ridge regression on ``train_years`` and predict ``test_year``.

    The scaler and the regularisation strength (cross-validated via ``RidgeCV``
    when ``alpha`` is ``None``) are determined from the training data only, then
    applied unchanged to the held-out year, so the test-year metrics are
    genuinely out of sample. Returns training/test sizes, the selected alpha,
    in-sample (train) RÂ², out-of-sample (test) RÂ², RMSE and MAE, the fitted
    coefficients, and the test-year observed and predicted values.
    """
    X_train, y_train = _prepare_xy(df, predictors, list(train_years))
    X_test, y_test = _prepare_xy(df, predictors, [test_year])

    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_train)
    X_train_std = scaler.transform(X_train)
    X_test_std = scaler.transform(X_test)

    if alpha is None:
        model = RidgeCV(alphas=RIDGE_ALPHAS).fit(X_train_std, y_train)
    else:
        model = Ridge(alpha=alpha).fit(X_train_std, y_train)

    y_pred = model.predict(X_test_std)

    ss_res = float(((y_test - y_pred) ** 2).sum())
    ss_tot = float(((y_test - y_test.mean()) ** 2).sum())
    r2_test = 1 - ss_res / ss_tot
    rmse = float(np.sqrt(((y_test.to_numpy() - y_pred) ** 2).mean()))
    mae = float(np.abs(y_test.to_numpy() - y_pred).mean())

    coefs = pd.DataFrame(
        [{"Term": "Intercept", "Coefficient": float(model.intercept_)}]
        + [
            {"Term": col, "Coefficient": float(coef)}
            for col, coef in zip(predictors, model.coef_)
        ]
    )

    return {
        "n_train": int(len(X_train)),
        "n_test": int(len(X_test)),
        "alpha": float(model.alpha_) if alpha is None else float(alpha),
        "r2_train": float(model.score(X_train_std, y_train)),
        "r2_test": float(r2_test),
        "rmse": rmse,
        "mae": mae,
        "coefs": coefs,
        "y_test": y_test.to_numpy(),
        "y_pred": y_pred,
    }

    """Cases complete on ``predictors`` and the target, applicable for all.

    """

def logistic_train_test(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    predictors: list[str],
    train_years: tuple[int, ...] = (2022, 2023, 2024),
    test_year: int = 2025,
    C: float = LOGISTIC_C,
) -> dict:
    """Fit a regularised logistic regression on ``train_years``, predict ``test_year``.

    Success is ``Sales_vs_Target_Pct >= SUCCESS_THRESHOLD``. The scaler is fit
    on the training data only and applied unchanged to the held-out year, so the
    test-year metrics are genuinely out of sample. Returns training/test sizes
    and success rates, the fitted coefficients (odds ratios), in-sample (train)
    and out-of-sample (test) classification metrics.
    """
    X_train, y_train_cont = _prepare_xy(df, predictors, list(train_years))
    X_test, y_test_cont = _prepare_xy(df, predictors, [test_year])

    y_train = (y_train_cont >= SUCCESS_THRESHOLD).astype(int)
    y_test = (y_test_cont >= SUCCESS_THRESHOLD).astype(int)

    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_train)
    X_train_std = scaler.transform(X_train)
    X_test_std = scaler.transform(X_test)

    model = LogisticRegression(
        C=C,
        l1_ratio=0.0,
        class_weight="balanced",
        solver="lbfgs",
        max_iter=2000,
    ).fit(X_train_std, y_train)

    y_prob_train = model.predict_proba(X_train_std)[:, 1]
    y_pred_train = model.predict(X_train_std)
    y_prob_test = model.predict_proba(X_test_std)[:, 1]
    y_pred_test = model.predict(X_test_std)

    coefs = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {
                "Term": "Intercept",
                "Coefficient": float(model.intercept_[0]),
                "Odds ratio": float(np.exp(model.intercept_[0])),
            }
        ]
        + [
            {
                "Term": col,
                "Coefficient": float(coef),
                "Odds ratio": float(np.exp(coef)),
            }
            for col, coef in zip(predictors, model.coef_[0])
        ]
    )

    return {
        "n_train": int(len(X_train)),
        "n_test": int(len(X_test)),
        "train_success_rate": float(y_train.mean() * 100),
        "test_success_rate": float(y_test.mean() * 100),
        "coefs": coefs,
        "train_accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_train, y_pred_train)),
        "train_balanced_accuracy": float(balanced_accuracy_score(y_train, y_pred_train)),
        "train_roc_auc": float(roc_auc_score(y_train, y_prob_train)),
        "test_accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred_test)),
        "test_balanced_accuracy": float(balanced_accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred_test)),
        "test_precision": float(precision_score(y_test, y_pred_test, zero_division=0)),
        "test_recall": float(recall_score(y_test, y_pred_test, zero_division=0)),
        "test_f1": float(f1_score(y_test, y_pred_test, zero_division=0)),
        "test_roc_auc": float(roc_auc_score(y_test, y_prob_test)),
    }

def _fold_classify(
    X_train: pd.DataFrame,
    y_train: np.ndarray,
    X_test: pd.DataFrame,
    y_test: np.ndarray,
    predictors: list[str],
    C: float,
) -> dict:
    """Fit a logistic model on one CV fold and score it on the held-out fold.

    Returns out-of-sample ROC-AUC, balanced accuracy and F1. ROC-AUC is NaN if
    the test fold holds a single class.
    """
    Xtr = X_train[predictors]
    Xte = X_test[predictors]
    scaler = StandardScaler().fit(Xtr)
    Xtr_std = scaler.transform(Xtr)
    Xte_std = scaler.transform(Xte)

    model = LogisticRegression(
        C=C,
        l1_ratio=0.0,
        class_weight="balanced",
        solver="lbfgs",
        max_iter=2000,
    ).fit(Xtr_std, y_train)

    y_prob = model.predict_proba(Xte_std)[:, 1]
    y_pred = model.predict(Xte_std)

    try:
        auc = float(roc_auc_score(y_test, y_prob))
    except ValueError:
        auc = float("nan")

    return {
        "auc": auc,
        "balanced_accuracy": float(balanced_accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)),
        "f1": float(f1_score(y_test, y_pred, zero_division=0)),
    }


def repeated_kfold_compare_logistic(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    base_predictors: list[str],
    full_predictors: list[str],
    C: float = LOGISTIC_C,
    n_splits: int = 7,
    n_repeats: int = 20,
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> dict:
    """Paired repeated K-fold comparison of two nested logistic models.

    Mirrors :func:`repeated_kfold_compare` for classification. Both models are
    fit on identical folds of the shared subset (cases complete on
    ``full_predictors``), so within-fold differences (full − base) isolate the
    contribution of the added predictors. Returns fold-level differences in
    ROC-AUC, balanced accuracy and F1 (all higher is better), plus each model's
    per-fold ROC-AUC.
    """
    sub = _shared_subset(df, full_predictors)
    X = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            col: pd.to_numeric(sub[col], errors="coerce")
            for col in full_predictors
        }
    )
    y = (
        pd.to_numeric(sub[TARGET], errors="coerce") >= SUCCESS_THRESHOLD
    ).astype(int).to_numpy()

    rkf = RepeatedKFold(
        n_splits=n_splits, n_repeats=n_repeats, random_state=random_state
    )

    auc_diff, bal_diff, f1_diff = [], [], []
    auc_base, auc_full = [], []
    for train_idx, test_idx in rkf.split(X):
        base = _fold_classify(
            X.iloc[train_idx],
            y[train_idx],
            X.iloc[test_idx],
            y[test_idx],
            base_predictors,
            C,
        )
        full = _fold_classify(
            X.iloc[train_idx],
            y[train_idx],
            X.iloc[test_idx],
            y[test_idx],
            full_predictors,
            C,
        )
        if np.isnan(base["auc"]) or np.isnan(full["auc"]):
            auc_diff.append(np.nan)
        else:
            auc_diff.append(full["auc"] - base["auc"])
        bal_diff.append(full["balanced_accuracy"] - base["balanced_accuracy"])
        f1_diff.append(full["f1"] - base["f1"])
        auc_base.append(base["auc"])
        auc_full.append(full["auc"])

    auc_diff = np.asarray(auc_diff, dtype=float)
    valid = ~np.isnan(auc_diff)

    return {
        "n_cases": int(len(sub)),
        "n_folds": n_splits * n_repeats,
        "n_folds_auc": int(valid.sum()),
        "auc_diff": auc_diff[valid],
        "bal_diff": np.asarray(bal_diff),
        "f1_diff": np.asarray(f1_diff),
        "auc_base": np.asarray(auc_base),
        "auc_full": np.asarray(auc_full),
    }

                f"{better_label} better (% of folds)": f"{s['p_positive'] * 100:.0f}",

        )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def plot_classification_cv_diffs(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    output_dir: str | Path | None = None,
    filename: str = "classification_cv_diffs.png",
) -> Path:
    """Histogram of fold-level classification metric differences.

    Two rows (implicit vs behavioural, behavioural vs survey) by three columns
    (ROC-AUC, balanced accuracy, F1). Each panel shows the distribution of
    within-fold (full − base) differences across the repeated K-fold splits,
    with the confidence interval shaded, a dashed line at zero, and a solid
    line at the mean.
    """
    output_dir = Path(output_dir) if output_dir is not None else log_writer.FIGURES_DIR
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    comparisons = [
        (
            modelling.BEHAVIOURAL_CV_PREDICTORS,
            modelling.IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS,
            "behavioural",
            "implicit",
        ),
        (
            modelling.SURVEY_MEASURES,
            modelling.BEHAVIOURAL_CV_PREDICTORS,
            "survey",
            "behavioural",
        ),
    ]
    metrics = [
        ("Δ ROC-AUC", "auc_diff", "ROC-AUC"),
        ("Δ balanced accuracy", "bal_diff", "balanced accuracy"),
        ("Δ F1", "f1_diff", "F1"),
    ]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 7.6))

    for row, (base, full, base_label, full_label) in enumerate(comparisons):
        res = modelling.repeated_kfold_compare_logistic(df, base, full)
        diff_label = f"{full_label} − {base_label}"
        for col, (metric_title, key, metric_label) in enumerate(metrics):
            ax = axes[row, col]
            diffs = res[key]
            s = modelling.summarise_fold_diffs(diffs)
            ax.axvspan(s["ci_lo"], s["ci_hi"], color="red", alpha=0.15, zorder=0)
            ax.hist(diffs, bins=25, color="#2c7fb8", alpha=0.85, edgecolor="white")
            ax.axvline(0, color="black", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.5)
            ax.axvline(s["mean"], color="black", linewidth=2)
            ax.text(
                0.03,
                0.97,
                f"mean = {s['mean']:+.3f}\n"
                f"95% CI [{s['ci_lo']:+.3f}, {s['ci_hi']:+.3f}]\n"
                f"{full_label} better: {s['p_positive'] * 100:.0f}% of folds",
                transform=ax.transAxes,
                va="top",
                ha="left",
                fontsize=9,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="white", ec="none", alpha=0.85),
            )
            ax.set_title(f"{diff_label}: {metric_title}", fontsize=11)
            if row == 1:
                ax.set_xlabel(f"Δ {metric_label}", fontsize=10)
            if col == 0:
                ax.set_ylabel("Folds", fontsize=10)

    fig.suptitle(
        "Repeated K-fold CV (classification): fold differences (full − base)",
        fontsize=13,
        y=0.99,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.97])

    path = output_dir / filename
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    return path

def plot_precision_recall(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    output_dir: str | Path | None = None,
    filename: str = "precision_recall.png",
) -> Path:
    """Precision-recall curves for the three models on the held-out 2025 concepts.

    Each panel shows the PR curve of one model (trained on 2022–2024, evaluated
    on 2025) alongside its no-skill baseline (the test-set success prevalence,
    shown as a dashed line) and its average precision (AP).
    """
    output_dir = Path(output_dir) if output_dir is not None else log_writer.FIGURES_DIR
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    models = [
        ("Survey", modelling.SURVEY_MEASURES, "#2c7fb8"),
        ("Survey + behavioural", modelling.BEHAVIOURAL_CV_PREDICTORS, "#31a354"),
        (
            "Survey + behavioural + implicit",
            modelling.IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS,
            "#e6550d",
        ),
    ]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.6), squeeze=False)

    for idx, (label, predictors, colour) in enumerate(models):
        res = modelling.logistic_train_test(df, predictors)
        y = res["y_test"]
        prob = res["y_prob_test"]

        precision, recall, _ = precision_recall_curve(y, prob)
        ap = float(average_precision_score(y, prob))
        prevalence = float(y.mean())

        ax = axes[0, idx]
        ax.step(recall, precision, where="post", color=colour, linewidth=2)
        ax.fill_between(recall, precision, step="post", color=colour, alpha=0.15)
        ax.axhline(prevalence, color="grey", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
        ax.text(
            0.55,
            0.05,
            f"AP = {ap:.3f}\nno-skill = {prevalence:.3f}\nn = {res['n_test']}",
            transform=ax.transAxes,
            va="bottom",
            ha="left",
            fontsize=9,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="white", ec="none", alpha=0.85),
        )
        ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
        ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
        ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")
        ax.set_title(f"{label} (n = {res['n_test']})", fontsize=11)
        ax.set_xlabel("Recall", fontsize=10)
        if idx == 0:
            ax.set_ylabel("Precision", fontsize=10)

    fig.suptitle(
        "Precision-recall on the held-out 2025 concepts (train 2022–2024)",
        fontsize=13,
        y=0.99,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.97])

    path = output_dir / filename
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    return path

def plot_calibration(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    output_dir: str | Path | None = None,
    filename: str = "calibration.png",
) -> Path:
    """Calibration curves for the three models on the held-out 2025 concepts.

    Each panel plots the model's mean predicted probability against the observed
    fraction of positives (bin-wise), with the diagonal marking perfect
    calibration, and annotates the Brier score.
    """
    output_dir = Path(output_dir) if output_dir is not None else log_writer.FIGURES_DIR
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    models = [
        ("Survey", modelling.SURVEY_MEASURES, "#2c7fb8"),
        ("Survey + behavioural", modelling.BEHAVIOURAL_CV_PREDICTORS, "#31a354"),
        (
            "Survey + behavioural + implicit",
            modelling.IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS,
            "#e6550d",
        ),
    ]

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.6), squeeze=False)

    for idx, (label, predictors, colour) in enumerate(models):
        res = modelling.logistic_train_test(df, predictors)
        y = res["y_test"]
        prob = res["y_prob_test"]

        fraction_pos, mean_pred = calibration_curve(y, prob, n_bins=5)

        ax = axes[0, idx]
        ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], color="grey", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
        ax.plot(mean_pred, fraction_pos, marker="o", color=colour, linewidth=2)
        ax.text(
            0.03,
            0.92,
            f"Brier score = {res['test_brier']:.3f}\nn = {res['n_test']}",
            transform=ax.transAxes,
            va="top",
            ha="left",
            fontsize=9,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="white", ec="none", alpha=0.85),
        )
        ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
        ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
        ax.set_aspect("equal", adjustable="box")
        ax.set_title(f"{label} (n = {res['n_test']})", fontsize=11)
        ax.set_xlabel("Mean predicted probability", fontsize=10)
        if idx == 0:
            ax.set_ylabel("Observed success frequency", fontsize=10)

    fig.suptitle(
        "Calibration on the held-out 2025 concepts (train 2022–2024)",
        fontsize=13,
        y=0.99,
    )
    fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.97])

    path = output_dir / filename
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    return path


if __name__ == "__main__":

"""Calibration curves for the three models on the held-out 2025 concepts.

    Each panel plots the model's mean predicted probability against the observed
    fraction of positives under two binning strategies — uniform-width bins and
    quantile bins — alongside the diagonal marking perfect calibration, and
    annotates the Brier score.

    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    models = [
        ("Survey", modelling.SURVEY_MEASURES, "#2c7fb8"),
        ("Survey + behavioural", modelling.BEHAVIOURAL_CV_PREDICTORS, "#31a354"),
        (

            modelling.IMPLICIT_CV_PREDICTORS,
            "#e6550d",
        ),
    ]
